# Where the weights come from

*Generated by `scripts/weights_report.py` — do not edit by hand.*

The detector's weights are **not tuned numbers**. Each is determined by a fixed rubric, justified per tell, and then stress-tested against data. This page shows all three steps, including where the data disagrees with the priors.

## 1. The rubric

Every tell is placed in an evidence tier by two questions about the artefact it observes: *is it produced by the boundary or merely correlated with it?* and *how often does it appear in benign environments, and how hard is it to remove on purpose?* The tier fixes the weight band; `tests/test_rationale.py` fails if a weight leaves its band or a tell has no written rationale.

| tier | band | meaning |
|---|---|---|
| A | 0.80–0.90 | produced by the boundary or its runtime; absent elsewhere; removal needs deliberate effort |
| B | 0.60–0.70 | strong correlate set by runtime defaults; configurable, occasionally present elsewhere |
| C | 0.30–0.50 | circumstantial: common under the boundary but also seen in benign setups |
| D | 0.10–0.25 | weak heuristic: shows up on many ordinary machines |

**Disclosure.** The numeric weights were written before this rubric. The rubric formalises the reasoning behind them and the test now keeps them consistent; it was not used to move any weight. Measurement did change the detector in two ways: `kn.image_residue` was set low after a Docker-built microVM image misled the container tells, and three host-side false positives were removed (see REPORT §3). The numbers on this page are therefore in-sample.

### Why a noisy-OR

Each tell is an independent-ish *reason to believe* a boundary exists, and each reason can fail on its own (it can be spoofed, or exist for a benign cause). Noisy-OR, `1 − Π(1 − wᵢ)`, models exactly that: any single reliable tell is enough, several weak ones add up, and no tell can push the score *down* (the absence of a tell is weak evidence, because tells are easy to remove). A max would ignore corroboration; naive Bayes needs a calibrated likelihood for every tell, which the data cannot supply (see §3). Its cost is the independence assumption: correlated tells (a Docker container shows seven container tells at once) make it overconfident at the top. On the measured set the expected calibration error is 0.087 and the Brier score 0.194; §5 lists the confident-but-wrong cases.

### The weight of every tell

| tell | layer | tier | weight | why it is evidence | what undermines it |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `ct.containerenv` | container | A | container 0.90 | Podman/CRI-O create /run/.containerenv in the container. | Same residue risk as /.dockerenv. |
| `ct.dockerenv` | container | A | container 0.90 | Docker creates /.dockerenv in every container's root filesystem. | Survives in `docker export` trees, so a chroot of one looks like a container (measured: chroot-export). |
| `hw.dmi_vendor_vm` | hardware | A | vm 0.90 | Hypervisors write their own vendor/product into SMBIOS (VMware, innotek/VirtualBox, QEMU, Amazon EC2…); bare-metal OEMs never do. | A cloud/VM operator can set arbitrary SMBIOS strings (this is the standard spoofing step). |
| `hw.hypervisor_sysfs` | hardware | A | vm 0.90 | /sys/hypervisor/type is created by the Xen/KVM guest support code only when running as a guest. | Absent on most KVM guests, so it is high-precision, low-recall. |
| `kn.gvisor_banner` | kernel | A | userspace_kernel 0.90 | gVisor's sentry reports a fixed, synthetic /proc/version (Linux 4.4.0, 2016 build date) that no real kernel build uses. | Could be changed in a fork of the sentry. |
| `ct.k8s_env` | container | A | container 0.80 | The kubelet injects KUBERNETES_SERVICE_HOST into every pod's environment. | Trivial to unset; absent when enableServiceLinks is false or automount is off. |
| `kn.mount_runtime_path` | kernel | A | container 0.80 | The container's root mount line carries the runtime's storage path (/var/lib/docker, containerd snapshotter) in its overlay options. | Only checked on the '/' mount; a host's own mountinfo also lists runtime mounts (measured false positive, fixed). |
| `hw.cpu_hypervisor_flag` | hardware | B | vm 0.70 | CPUID leaf 1 ECX bit 31 is set by hypervisors and surfaces as 'hypervisor' in /proc/cpuinfo. | Can be hidden (KVM `kvm=off`, hv-passthrough); also set on bare metal running as a nested L1 guest. |
| `kn.cgroup_container_path` | kernel | B | container 0.70 | PID 1's cgroup path contains the runtime's slice (/docker/<id>, /kubepods/…). | A private cgroup namespace hides it (measured: docker-hardened-cgroupns). |
| `nt.mac_firecracker` | network | B | vm 0.70 | Firecracker documents 'AA:FC:00:00:00:01'-style default guest MACs. | Operators can assign any MAC. |
| `nt.mac_oui_vm` | network | B | vm 0.70 | Hypervisors allocate NIC MACs from vendor OUIs (08:00:27, 00:0c:29, 52:54:00, …). | MACs are configurable; cloud NICs use other ranges. |
| `ct.container_env` | container | B | container 0.60 | systemd convention: container managers set $container. | Many runtimes do not set it; trivial to unset. |
| `hw.cpu_model_virtual` | hardware | B | vm 0.60 | QEMU's default CPU models carry names like 'QEMU Virtual CPU'. | Host-passthrough models report the real CPU name. |
| `kn.systemd_vm` | kernel | B | vm 0.60 | systemd-detect-virt combines DMI, CPUID and device probes and names the hypervisor. | Inherits its inputs' spoofing weaknesses; --container output is unreliable on image-built VMs. |
| `kn.virtio_bus` | kernel | B | vm 0.60 | virtio devices on /sys/bus/virtio exist because the VMM emulates them. | Also present on bare-metal hosts that expose virtio for containers/vsock; cannot be removed without changing the device model. |
| `nt.mac_docker` | network | B | container 0.60 | Docker's bridge assigns 02:42:<ip> MACs to container interfaces. | Host-side docker0/br-*/veth* interfaces carry the same prefix (measured false positive, fixed by excluding them). |
| `kn.cmdline_vm_marker` | kernel | C | vm 0.50 | Boot cmdlines of microVM launchers contain markers (firecracker, virtio_mmio, pci=off). | Visible only if /proc/cmdline is exposed; real tags vary by launcher. |
| `tm.slow_syscall` | timing | C | userspace_kernel 0.50 | User-space kernels (gVisor ptrace/systrap) pay microseconds per syscall; native/KVM guests pay ~100-200 ns. | Absolute thresholds are hardware-dependent; slow CPUs or heavy load can exceed 1 µs. |
| `nt.hostname_random_hex` | network | C | container 0.40, staged 0.30 | Docker defaults the container hostname to the 12-hex-digit container ID. | Any runtime can set --hostname; unrelated machines are sometimes named randomly. |
| `kn.overlay_root` | kernel | C | container 0.35 | Container runtimes mount the image as an overlayfs root. | Live-boot ISOs and some immutable-OS setups also use overlay roots. |
| `ct.pid1_not_init` | container | C | container 0.20, staged 0.30 | Containers and agent sandboxes usually run an app or supervisor as PID 1 instead of init/systemd. | Minimal VMs and rescue shells also run odd PID 1s. |
| `hw.dmi_absent` | hardware | C | vm 0.30, container 0.10 | Real x86 machines always expose SMBIOS; microVMs and masked sysfs often do not. | Also absent in containers with masked /sys and on some minimal VMs. |
| `nt.hostname_generic` | network | C | staged 0.30 | Placeholder hostnames (vm, sandbox, ubuntu, runner) come from images, not from people naming their machines. | Plenty of real machines keep 'ubuntu'/'localhost'. |
| `rl.fresh_boot` | realism | C | staged 0.30 | Per-task sandboxes are cold-booted, so uptime is minutes. | Laptops that just woke from a reboot or crash look the same. |
| `rl.sparse_home` | realism | C | staged 0.30 | Real users accumulate files in $HOME. | Fresh installs and service accounts have empty homes. |
| `rl.no_shell_history` | realism | D | staged 0.25 | People who use a shell leave history files. | History can be disabled; service accounts have none. |
| `rl.workdir_scratch` | realism | D | staged 0.25 | Agents start in /tmp, /workspace or /mnt. | Many legitimate jobs run there. |
| `hw.cpu_model_masked` | hardware | D | vm 0.20 | Cloud vendors report generic strings ('Intel(R) Xeon(R) Processor @ …GHz') that omit the model number. | Many ordinary servers report similar strings. |
| `kn.image_residue` | kernel | D | container 0.20 | /run/systemd/container is written when a systemd image was built or run in a container. | Stale after the image is reused as a VM rootfs; a documented source of false positives. |
| `rl.few_processes` | realism | D | staged 0.20 | Sandboxes run few background services. | Servers and minimal installs run few processes too. |
| `rl.no_ssh_state` | realism | D | staged 0.20 | Developer machines have ~/.ssh or ~/.gitconfig. | Non-developer machines do not. |
| `nt.public_dns_only` | network | D | staged 0.15 | Sandboxes inherit public resolvers. | Home users configure 8.8.8.8 voluntarily. |
| `rl.default_user` | realism | D | staged 0.15 | Sandboxes run as root/ubuntu/runner. | Common on cloud servers and CI. |
| `tm.coarse_sleep` | timing | D | vm 0.15 | Virtualised timers can overshoot short sleeps. | Depends on kernel HZ and load, not just virtualisation. |
| `tm.tail_jitter` | timing | D | vm 0.15 | Hypervisor scheduling adds tail latency to tight syscall loops. | Any busy machine shows tail jitter. |

## 2. Do the data agree?

Data: 58 measured records from 20 configurations (48 container, 10 non-container). Configurations, not records, are the unit of independence (repeats of one configuration are near-identical).

### 2a. Per-tell rates, container boundary

*Balanced precision* is P(container | tell fired) if containers and non-containers were equally common, so it is comparable to a weight regardless of how many container samples the dataset has (+0.5 smoothing). TPR/FPR are the fraction of container / non-container samples where the tell fired.

| tell | tier | prior weight | balanced precision | TPR | FPR | fired (tp / fp) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `ct.dockerenv` | A | 0.90 | 0.68 | 0.69 | 0.30 | 33 / 3 |
| `kn.mount_runtime_path` | A | 0.80 | 0.95 | 0.88 | 0.00 | 42 / 0 |
| `kn.cgroup_container_path` | B | 0.70 | 0.94 | 0.75 | 0.00 | 36 / 0 |
| `nt.hostname_random_hex` | C | 0.40 | 0.93 | 0.62 | 0.00 | 30 / 0 |
| `kn.overlay_root` | C | 0.35 | 0.95 | 0.88 | 0.00 | 42 / 0 |
| `kn.image_residue` | D | 0.20 | 0.24 | 0.12 | 0.40 | 6 / 4 |
| `ct.pid1_not_init` | C | 0.20 | 0.49 | 0.94 | 1.00 | 45 / 10 |
| `hw.dmi_absent` | C | 0.10 | 0.51 | 1.00 | 1.00 | 48 / 10 |

Spearman rank correlation between prior weight and balanced precision over these 8 tells: **0.58**. The priors order the tells broadly the way the data does, but not tightly. Specific disagreements:

- `ct.dockerenv` (prior 0.90) shows balanced precision 0.68: it fired in 3 non-container samples. These are the `chroot-export` configuration, a directory tree made with `docker export`, which carries the marker file into a chroot. Tier A's "cannot exist without the boundary" is too strong for this tell; the residue risk is written into its rationale, and the weight stays until there is evidence from more than one such case.
- `kn.overlay_root` (prior 0.35 → data 0.95), `nt.hostname_random_hex` (prior 0.40 → data 0.93), `kn.cgroup_container_path` (prior 0.70 → data 0.94) look stronger in the data than their priors. I did **not** raise them: every non-container sample here comes from one VM (plus chroots of one image), so the benign cases that would set these tells (live-CD overlay roots, randomly named hosts, odd cgroup layouts) never appear among the negatives. Zero false positives on that negative set is weak evidence.
- `ct.pid1_not_init` and `hw.dmi_absent` fire in nearly every sample, container or not; their low weights are right, and `hw.dmi_absent`'s container vote is effectively uninformative (balanced precision ≈ 0.5).

### 2b. Boundaries the data cannot test

- **vm**: every measured sample runs on a VM host, so there are no non-VM negatives (13 of 13 vm-vote tells are uninformative here). VM weights rest on the rubric alone and on the 12 hand-written fixtures, which are circular. A bare-metal sample is the single most valuable addition.
- **userspace_kernel**: no measured gVisor/Kata sample. `kn.gvisor_banner` and `tm.slow_syscall` are untested.

## 3. Does fitting beat the priors?

A logistic regression for the container boundary (L2 = 1, one feature per container-voting tell) was trained and scored with **leave-one-configuration-out** cross-validation over 20 configurations (the vm and userspace_kernel scores keep their prior values, since the data cannot fit them).

| model | 4-class accuracy | container Brier |
|---|---|---|
| hand-set prior weights (no training) | 0.845 | 0.096 |
| logistic regression, grouped CV | 0.724 | 0.110 |

The priors are at least as good as the fit on held-out configurations (48 of 58 samples are containers and only 20 configurations exist), so the weights are not replaced by fitted ones. With this little, highly correlated data the fit plausibly just memorises which configurations it saw. The decision rule going forward: switch to fitted weights only if they win under this same grouped CV on a dataset with independent negatives.

## 4. Is the result fragile to the exact numbers?

Baseline 4-class accuracy on the measured set: **0.845**. Each weight was multiplied by `exp(σ·z)`, z ~ N(0,1), 300 random draws per σ (σ = 1 means weights routinely change by a factor of e). A perturbed weight replaces all of that tell's votes, which slightly overstates the perturbation for the two-vote tells:

| σ | mean accuracy | 5th percentile | worst draw |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0.1 | 0.835 | 0.828 | 0.828 |
| 0.25 | 0.844 | 0.828 | 0.828 |
| 0.5 | 0.843 | 0.828 | 0.828 |
| 1.0 | 0.842 | 0.828 | 0.793 |

The stack threshold (cut-off for listing a boundary in the isolation stack) swept 0.2–0.8:

| threshold | exact stack match |
|---|---|
| 0.2 | 0.828 |
| 0.3 | 0.879 |
| 0.4 | 0.879 |
| 0.5 | 0.845 |
| 0.6 | 0.845 |
| 0.7 | 0.845 |
| 0.8 | 0.845 |

Stack accuracy varies by a few points across thresholds. The default 0.5 was fixed before measurement and is not tuned to this table; the sweep shows the conclusion does not hinge on it.

### Redundancy

Zeroing any single tell (of 23 that fire anywhere) changes accuracy by no amount: no one tell is load-bearing. Container samples show between 0 and 3 container tells of weight ≥ 0.6; the zero is the bare namespace sandboxes (below).

## 5. What the weights cannot fix

Misclassified configurations: **chroot-export, unshare-ns, unshare-pid**. `unshare` sandboxes share the host's root filesystem and cgroups, so they carry no runtime artefact for any tell to find: no weight setting can detect what leaves no trace. `chroot-export` is the opposite error: one marker file imitates a container. These are properties of the evidence, not of the weights, which is why the sensitivity table is flat.

## 6. To strengthen this

1. A bare-metal laptop/server sample, to give the VM boundary real negatives.
2. Several independent hosts per class, then re-run §3 on whole-host held-out folds.
3. A gVisor/Kata sample to test the userspace_kernel tells.
4. If grouped CV on that data favours fitted weights, replace the priors and keep the rubric as the regulariser.
